main_text.p: ces.Hoc certè elephantis genus in minore Britannia ob immoderatum pifcium reces- tium efum grassatur, adoriturq; quofdam homines, quos nostri Galli ladres blancs, uocant, qui quidè à cæteris excludi solent. Caufam uero antecedentem habet pitui- tam putrefastam, queamdmodum ex colo- re licet conijcere. Etenim color efflorefcit semper similis humoribus redundantibus in corpore, nifi intrinsecus refluxerint. Deinde id satis declarat elleborus albus, qui purgandæ pituitæ crassæ potentissimam uim possidet. Duæ autem aliæ elephantis species facilè discernuntur. Quæ enim ue- lut cancer occultus est, à Cornelio Celso e- Cap.25.gregiè describitur libro de re Medica ter- tio, ubi addit totum corpus affici: ita ut os- sa quoq; uitiari dicantur. Summa (inquit) pars corporis crebras maculas, crebrosq; tumores habet: rubor harum paulatim in atrum colorem conuertitur. Summa cutis inæqualiter crassa, tenuis, dura, mollisque quasi squamis quibusdam exasperatur, cor- pus emacrefcit, oss, furę, pedes intumescut. Vbi uetus morbus est, digiti in manibus pe- dibusq; sub tumore conduntur, febricula oritur, quæ facilè tot malis obrutum homi- nem.

page.notes: Marginal reference "Cap.25." is a running-text marginal note at the left, beside the paragraph; it is shown in the note element with letter "25" as a section reference. Some words are damaged by the scan (the "ces." at the top of the line may be the tail of a previous word; "s" long s has been normalised to plain s per rule 5, so "satis", "semper" etc. appear as s). The original text ends with "nem'" at the right margin, a catchword-like fragment ("nem'") placed at the right below the last line; it is the continuation of "hominem" and is kept as the end of the text. Possible printing errors left as printed: "Summa (inquit)", "oss" for ossa, "furę" for surae, "intumescut" for intumescunt, "squamis", "quasi" as printed in the scan. Words with uncertain letters in the scan are not individually marked; the letters "ces." and "nem'" are cut from adjacent words.
